messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Patient Information:
Name: [redacted]
Age: 39
Gender: Male
Date of Admission: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Hospital Course Summary:
The patient was admitted to Tri-Service General Hospital with multiple injuries including rib fractures, pelvic fracture with active bleeding, and dissection of the descending aorta with intramural hematoma caused by a fall from a fifth floor window. The patient underwent bilateral anterior thoracotomies and transcatheter embolization of the pelvic vessels for acute resuscitation. The patient then received thoracic endovascular aortic repair of the descending aortic aneurysm which was followed by oxygen desaturation and cardiac arrest. Advanced cardiac life support was performed immediately and the patient was placed on ECMO due to persistent bradycardia. Though diagnosed with brain death a few days later, the family decided to donate the patient's organs.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Course of Treatment:
Following informed consent, both recipients received dialysis within the first postoperative week due to delayed graft function. Immunosuppressive therapy was used to treat the two patients. The SCr of the recipients decreased from 8.5 and 17.6 mg/dL to 1.1 and 1.8 mg/dL, respectively, at the 1-month postoperative follow-up. The grafts remained functional at the 8-month follow-up.

Follow-up Plan:
The patients were advised to follow up with their respective nephrologists to monitor their kidney function and progress.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for admission is the traumatic injury of the descending thoracic aorta (dissection with intramural haematoma) from the fall. It is the most severe of the multiple injuries and drove the TEVAR and the subsequent arrest. This places it in the injury chapter S, category S25 (injury of blood vessels of thorax), sequenced ahead of the pelvic (S32) and rib (S22) fractures.

CODE: S25
